A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Scaling Up Masked Diffusion Models on Text. All 24 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original scaling experiments, language-understanding evaluations, conditional-generation results, reversal and temporal-shift experiments, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices; they are not solely results attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: The masked diffusion formulation, architecture, training objective, unsupervised classifier-free guidance and inference procedures are unchanged, including the greedy sampling algorithm in Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training and evaluation coverage: SlimPajama, language-understanding benchmarks, GSM8K, ShareGPT/MT-Bench, fictitious reversal tasks and temporally shifted FineWeb data. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments, including GPT-2, TinyLlama and Llama-2 in Table 2, the ARM in Table 4, GPT-3/Llama-2/T5 in Table 5, and the CFG comparison methods.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, preprocessing, metrics and testing procedures are unchanged. The abstract's explicit 16-fold pre-training-time qualification repeats the setting already stated in v2 Section 6 and Table 4; it does not establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The CFG ablations, train-test discrepancy controls, likelihood-estimation comparisons, scaling analyses, temporal robustness tests and generated examples are retained unchanged, including Appendix C and Figures 3–6.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Both retain the same Monte Carlo estimation descriptions and sample counts in Appendix B.2 and Table 11; no seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval or significance-test reporting is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and generated examples are unchanged throughout both versions. For example, Table 4 retains the MDM score of 1.56 at 396 seconds and ARM score of 1.57 at 555 seconds under the same stated conditions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the scaling-law formulation and mathematical reasoning supporting unsupervised CFG are unchanged. No definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly qualifies the 1.4-times speed advantage as occurring during sampling with 16 times more pre-training time. It also omits the higher-quality-at-higher-cost branch from its summary, although that claim remains in the introduction and Section 6. Other core claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Scientific interpretations and limitations are unchanged. The abstract repeats an existing training-cost qualification, while the new ethics statement supplies generic misinformation and bias caveats rather than a substantive analysis of this work's limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, model configurations and code/data access information remain unchanged, including Appendix B and Tables 7–9. The abstract's training-cost statement was already disclosed elsewhere in v2.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior diffusion and autoregressive models are unchanged. The bibliography is reflowed without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v3 makes a localized abstract revision, adds an ethics statement and funding acknowledgments, removes the acknowledgments section number, and changes the preprint header to ICLR 2025 publication status. The scientific narrative and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Publication headers and the layout of the ethics, acknowledgments and reference pages change. All six figures, fifteen tables and Algorithm 1 retain their displays and placement; there is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency by stating the 16-fold pre-training-time cost alongside the abstract's 1.4-times sampling-speed claim, aligning the headline comparison with the existing Section 6 and Table 4 evidence. This is a useful but limited clarification; the methods, empirical support and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
